titleEn: The Secret History of the Mongols — §§196–197: The fall of the Naiman, and Qulan Qatun
part: §§196–197 — The fall of the Naiman, and Qulan Qatun

sentences.t: Žamuqa Tajaṅ Qān-a ede üges ein üġüleġed
sentences.l: Žamuqa, to Tajaṅ Qān these words thus having said,
sentences.i: Jamuqa, having spoken these words to Tayang Qan,
sentences.n: Read ede üges ein üġüleġed as “these words thus having said”: -ġed is the converb of a finished action, and the Ming 這般 for ein, “in this manner”, points back at what Jamuqa has just told Tayang in §195. Qān-a is the short form of the title (qaγan) with the dative-locative -a, which the Ming writes 行, “to”. The sentence does not end here: a converb chain begins, and it is broken into units at the places marked below.

morph.gloss: Tayang, a man's name (the Naiman ruler) [人名]
qan, sovereign (short form beside qaγan) [皇帝行]
dative-locative: at, in, to (back-vowel form; the Ming marks it 行) [皇帝行]
converb of completed action: having …-ed [說了]

sentences.t: Naiman-(n)ača qaγačan bölde idču γarču
sentences.l: from the Naiman parting, apart dividing, going out,
sentences.i: he broke away from the Naiman, split off, and went out,
sentences.n: Three converbs in -n / -ču hang on the finite verb that comes later: qaγačan “parting”, idču “dividing”, γarču “going out”. The ablative -(n)ača is “from”. bölde is the doubtful word: the Ming gives it only the rare character 𠮠, which glosses öġere “apart” elsewhere, so “apart” is a guess; and id- is a stem inferred from the Ming 分着 “dividing”. The subject (Jamuqa) is carried over from the last unit.

morph.gloss: the Naiman, a people [種名 處]
apart, separately (uncertain; the Ming gives only the rare character 𠮠, which glosses öġere 'apart' elsewhere; no stem offered) [𠮠]
to divide, to split off (stem inferred from the Ming 分着) [分着]

sentences.t: Čiṅgis Qaγan-(n)a kele oroγ̇ulžu ilerün anda-da ügüle keġen ügüležü ilerün:
sentences.l: to Chinggis Qaγan word making-enter, sending, to the sworn brother say, saying, speaking, sending:
sentences.i: He sent word to Chinggis Qahan, charging the messenger to say it to his sworn brother, and sent him off with these words:
sentences.n: oroγ̇ulžu is oro- “enter” + causative -γ̇ul- + converb -žu, “making (the word) enter”; the Ming 敎入着 reads the same way. anda-da ügüle keġen is an instruction formula: the bare stem ügüle “say!” (the Ming 說 reads it as a plain stem) and keġen “saying”, closing the quotation. The envoy is never named; “charging the messenger” is supplied from the sense. ilerün (twice; the Ming glosses the first 去時, the second only 去) is ile- “send” with -rün, “when / while sending”; with the Ming’s 去 “go” a reading “going” is also possible (uncertain). The colon is Shiratori’s.

morph.gloss: dative-locative: at, in, to (back-vowel form; the (n) is Shiratori’s, printed after a stem ending in n; the Ming marks it 行) [皇帝 行]
converb of time: when, while [去時]
sworn brother, pledged friend [契合 行]
dative-locative: to, at (back-vowel form) [契合 行]
to speak, to say; the bare stem, 'say!' (stem used as imperative) [說]

sentences.t: "Tajaṅ Qān üge-dür min-u üküdġüžü öġede temečen ürġüžü γarba.
sentences.l: “Tajaṅ Qān, in the word my dazed, high struggling, frightened, went up.
sentences.i: “Tayang Qan, dazed by my words, frightened and struggling upward, has gone up.
sentences.n: Jamuqa’s message begins; Shiratori’s opening quotation mark is on Tajaṅ. üge-dür is “in / at the word”, the dative-locative -dür written 行/裏 by the Ming, here “by my words”; min-u “my” is the genitive of bi, set after its noun like in-ü. Three converbs lead to γarba “went up”. Uncertain: üküdġü- is a stem read from the Ming 昏着 “dazed”, ürġü- from 驚着 “frightened”, and öġede temečen (Ming 高 爭, “high”, “contend”) is rendered “struggling upward” by guess.

morph.gloss: dative-locative: in, at (front-vowel form) [言語 裏]
my, of me (bi, genitive stem min- + -u, set after its noun) [我的]
to be dazed, bewildered (stem inferred from the Ming 昏着 'dim, dazed') [昏着]
up, high (Ming 高 'high'; elsewhere 'upstream, upon') [高]
to be frightened (stem inferred from the Ming 驚着) [驚着]
to go out, to go up [上了]

sentences.t: Ama-γ̇ar alaγdažu ajužu aγ̇ula abarin γarba.
sentences.l: With the mouth being killed, fearing, the mountain climbing, went up.
sentences.i: Afraid of being killed by mere words, he climbed the mountain.
sentences.n: ama-γ̇ar is “with the mouth” (instrumental -γ̇ar; the Ming 敎口 glosses it as “mouth”), and alaγdažu is ala- “kill” + passive -γda- + converb, “being killed”. “Killed by the mouth” I take as “by (mere) words”, but that idiom is uncertain, and so is the passive, whose stem ala- is inferred. The rest is converbs again (ajužu “fearing”, abarin “climbing”, from the Ming 登) and γarba, “went up” (γar- is both “go out” and “go up”).

morph.gloss: to climb (Ming 登; stem inferred) [登]
to go out, to go up [上了]

sentences.t: Anda qadaγ̇uči; müd aγ̇ula-dur γarba.
sentences.l: Anda cautious; they in the mountain went up.
sentences.i: Anda, take care: they have gone up into the mountain.
sentences.n: anda is the sworn brother, here the one addressed. qadaγ̇uči carries the Ming 謹慎 “careful, cautious”; I take it as an address (“[be] watchful”), but it could equally be a statement about Chinggis, and the form itself is not secure. müd “they” (Ming 他每, the form uncertain) and aγ̇ula-dur, “in / into the mountain”, with dative-locative -dur written 行 by the Ming.

morph.gloss: one on guard, a careful one (Ming 謹慎 'careful, cautious'; perhaps an agent noun in -či; the stem is not certain) [謹︀愼]
they (third-person plural; the exact form is uncertain) [他每]
dative-locative: at, in, to (back-vowel form) [山 裏]
to go out, to go up [上了]

sentences.t: Ede esergülekü čirai ügeigün bi.
sentences.l: These to-oppose countenance without are.
sentences.i: They have no face to meet us with.
sentences.n: esergülekü is a participle, “to face, to oppose”, from a stem esergüle- inferred from the Ming 迎, “to meet head-on”; čirai ügeigün is “face-without”. The ending of ügeigün is uncertain: the glossary has read it as plural -gün (“those without”), and ede “these” agrees, but the Ming 無 shows no plural. bi here is the plain “is” (Ming 有). “Face to meet us with” takes liberties with “countenance to oppose”; the sense, no courage to face us, is clear enough.

morph.gloss: to face, to meet head-on, to oppose (stem inferred from the Ming 迎) [迎的]
ending of uncertain force (perhaps plural, 'those without'; the Ming 無 shows no plural) [無]
is, exists (perhaps a short form of bü-; Ming 有) [有]

sentences.t: Bi bürün Naiman-(n)ača qaγačaba" keġežü iležüġüi.
sentences.l: I, being, from the Naiman parted.” saying, sent.
sentences.i: “As for me, I have parted from the Naiman.” So he said, and sent it off.
sentences.n: bi bürün is “I, being”, and the Ming 呵 on bürün is its usual marker of “as for …”. qaγačaba is qaγača- “part” in the past -ba; the closing quotation mark is on it. keġežü iležüġüi, “saying, sent”, closes the message: -žüġüi is a past ending (front-vowel form), and the Ming 去了 reads ile- as “went”; “sent” is the reading used for ile- elsewhere in this part, which leaves the Ming’s “went” uncertain.

morph.gloss: converb: being; after a pronoun 'as for …' (Ming 呵) [呵]
the Naiman, a people [種名 處]
to part, separate, break away [分離了]
past: -ed (front-vowel form; the Ming 去了 reads 'went') [去了]

sentences.t: Čiṅgis Qaγan naran žilda boldažu Naqu gun-(n)u aγ̇ula-ji büselgün baižu qonoba.
sentences.l: Chinggis Qaγan, the sun late having become, of Naqu crag the mountain-(object) encircling standing, spent the night.
sentences.i: At dusk Chinggis Qahan set a ring about the mountain of Naqu Crag and stopped there for the night.
sentences.n: naran žilda boldažu is “the sun, having been made late” (žilda, from the Ming 晩, is uncertain; bolda- is a passive-looking stem). Naqu gun-(n)u aγ̇ula-ji is “Naqu Crag’s mountain” with the accusative -ji, the Ming writing 山名 (Naqu) 崖的 山行, “mountain-name, crag’s, mountain”. büselgün baižu (Ming 圍 立着, “surrounding, standing”) is the besieger’s ring; the stem of büselgün is not secure. qonoba is qono- “spend the night” in the past. The subject is Chinggis all the way through.

morph.gloss: late, evening (read from the Ming 晩; uncertain) [晩]
to be made, to become (passive; stem uncertain) [被做着]
genitive: of (back-vowel form; the (n) is Shiratori’s, printed after a stem that already ends in n) [崖的]
accusative (after a vowel): marks the object (Ming 行) [山行]
ring, encirclement, 'surrounding' (Ming 圍; stem uncertain) [圍]

sentences.t: Tere süni Naiman buruγ̇uilan ködölkün bolun
sentences.l: That night the Naiman slipping away, moving, being,
sentences.i: That night the Naiman, slipping away, were on the move,
sentences.n: The sentence is long and is broken in two here. buruγ̇uilan is a converb from a stem read off the Ming 𧻞避着, “dodging, avoiding”; ködölkün bolun is “being movers”, with an ending -kün that I cannot place (the Ming 每 suggests a plural) and bolun “becoming” (the Ming 做). The sense I take is that they were on the move, slipping away from the ring; the idiomatic line adds no “trying” and no “began”, for bolun is plain “being”.

morph.gloss: to go astray, to slip away, to evade (stem inferred from the Ming 𧻞避着 'dodging, avoiding') [𧻞避着]
to move, to set out [動每]
ending of uncertain force forming a noun or plural participle (Ming 每 'plural'): 'those moving' [動每]

sentences.t: Naqu deġerēče γuladču deġere deġere-ġen qutaγlaldužu jasu hüšü-ben kemkerü unaldužu qunžiγ̇u baitala darulčažu üküldüžüġüi.
sentences.l: from above Naqu falling, above above-own heaping up together, bones hair-own broken, falling together, rotten wood until pressing upon one another, died together.
sentences.i: Falling from the top of Naqu, they piled on one another, their bones and hair broken to pieces, crushing each other until they were like rotten wood, and all died together.
sentences.n: A chain of converbs in -žu with the joint or reciprocal -ldu- “together / one another” (qutaγlaldužu, unaldužu), ending in the finite üküldüžüġüi, which carries the same -ldu- (the converb darulčažu has a related joint ending, -lča-, uncertain): the Ming says 共 “together” and 相 “one another” throughout. deġerēče is deġere “above” with the ablative -ēče, “from the top”; deġere-ġen is “on their own above”, I read as “upon one another” (Ming (自的行)). hüšü is “hair” by the Ming 髮, so jasu hüšü-ben is “bones and hair”. Uncertain: qunžiγ̇u (Ming (爛木), “rotten wood”) and baitala (Ming 直到, “right up to”), which I render “until … like rotten wood”; kemkerü “broken” and the stems γulad-, qutaγla- are read from the Ming.

morph.gloss: ablative: from (front-vowel form, long ē) [上處]
to fall, to drop (stem inferred from the Ming 墜着) [墜着]
above, upper, on top [上(自的)行]
reflexive-possessive: one's own (Ming (自的行)), 'on one another' [上(自的)行]
to heap, to pile up (stem inferred from the Ming (堆積着)) [(堆積着)]
reflexive-possessive: one's own (front-vowel form) [髮自的行]
broken to pieces, crushed (Ming 碎; stem uncertain, perhaps a converb in -ü) [碎]
rotten wood (the Ming gives it in brackets, (爛木); uncertain) [(爛木)]
right up to, until (Ming 直到; perhaps bai- 'stand' + -tala 'until'; uncertain) [直到]
to press upon one another (Ming 相壓着; perhaps daru- 'press' + a joint ending) [相壓着]

sentences.t: Manaγaši in-ü Tajaṅ Qān-i muqudγažu abuba.
sentences.l: Tomorrow-toward his Tajaṅ Qān-(object) driving to the end took.
sentences.i: The next morning they drove Tayang Qan to extremity and took him.
sentences.n: manaγaši is “toward tomorrow” (the Ming 明早 gives it as “tomorrow morning”; the r of manaγar is dropped), so “the next morning”. muqudγažu is “wiping out, driving to the end” (the Ming 窮極着 “to the extreme”; the stem is likely, not certain); abuba is ab- “take” in the past. in-ü is “his”, but I cannot say whom it points to (the Ming 他的 only says “his”); the “they” of the idiomatic line is Chinggis’s men, supplied, and “his” is left out there.

morph.gloss: directive: toward (written manaγaši, the r dropped) [明早]
his, her, its (third-person genitive, placed after its noun) [他的]
accusative: marks the object (-i after a consonant; Ming 行) [皇帝行]
to wipe out, to drive to the end (stem likely; Ming 窮極 'to the extreme') [窮極着]

sentences.t: Küčülüg Qān öġere aγsaγ̇ar čüġen küġün daižin ködölžü güjičegderün Tamir-a küreġeležüġü.
sentences.l: Küčülüg Qān apart being, few man hostile moving, when overtaken, at the Tamir ring-formed.
sentences.i: Küchülüg Qan, who had been apart, with a few men, in revolt and on the move, when overtaken at the Tamir drew his camp into a ring.
sentences.n: öġere aγsaγ̇ar is “while being apart” (öġere with the rare Ming character 𠮠; aγsaγ̇ar, Ming 住間 “while dwelling”, is a- “be” with a participle and the instrumental -γ̇ar, a form I do not fully analyse). daižin ködölžü is “turning hostile, moving”, the Ming 反 “rebelling”. güjičegderün is a passive converb of time, “when overtaken” (Ming 被趕上時). Tamir-a: the Ming 河名 行 marks Tamir as a river and the -a as “at”. küreġeležüġü, “circle-made” (Ming 劄圈子有), is a camp drawn up in a ring; the ending is -žüġü, the usual past -žüġüi without its i.

morph.gloss: participle stem (as in -γsad, -γsan): having been [住間]
to turn against, to turn hostile (from dain 'enemy'; Ming 反) [反着]
to move, to set in motion [動着]
to chase, to overtake (stem inferred from the Ming 趕上) [被趕上時]
converb of time: when, while [被趕上時]
the Tamir, a river name (Ming 河名) [河名 行]
dative-locative: at, in, to (back-vowel form; the Ming marks it 行) [河名 行]
past: -ed (= -žüġüi, printed without the i) [劄圈子有]

sentences.t: Tere küreġen-dür(i)-jen bain jadažü ködölžü dutaγ̇ažu γarču odba.
sentences.l: That in the ring own standing unable, moving, fleeing, going out, went.
sentences.i: Unable to stand in that ring of his, he moved off, fled, broke out, and went away.
sentences.n: küreġen-dür(i)-jen is küreġen “ring”, the dative-locative -dür (front-vowel form) and the reflexive-possessive -jen, “in his own ring”; the (i) is Shiratori’s linking vowel, and the Ming 圈子 自的行 reads the -jen as 自的 “own”. bain jadažü is jada- “be unable” (Ming 不能着) after a verb, “unable to stand”; then three more converbs, and odba “went”. The subject is Küchülüg.

morph.gloss: dative-locative: in, at (front-vowel form) [圈子 自的行]
reflexive-possessive: one's own (front-vowel form; the (i) before it is Shiratori's linking vowel) [圈子 自的行]
to be unable (Ming 不能) [不能着]
to move, to set in motion [動着]
to go out, to go up [出着]

sentences.t: Naiman irgen-ü ulus-i Altai-jin ölgede muqudγažu qurijaba.
sentences.l: The Naiman people’s realm-(object), at the Altai’s foot, driving to the end, gathered in.
sentences.i: At the foot of the Altai he drove the realm of the Naiman people to extremity and gathered it in.
sentences.n: The subject is not stated; I take it to be Chinggis, who has just run Tayang to ground. irgen-ü ulus-i is “the people’s realm” with the accusative -i. Altai-jin ölgede: ölgede, from the Ming 山前 “in front of the mountain”, I read as “at the foot”; the stem ölge- is uncertain. muqudγažu is the same “wiping out / driving to the end” as in the unit about Tayang Qan; qurijaba is “gathered in” (Ming 收了), stem inferred.

morph.gloss: people, the common folk of a camp or realm [百姓 的]
genitive: of (front-vowel form, after n) [百姓 的]
accusative: marks the object (after a consonant) [國 行]
genitive: of (after a vowel) [山名 的]
front, foot of a mountain (Ming 山前; stem uncertain) [山前(行)]
to wipe out, to drive to the end [窮極着]
to gather in, to assemble (Ming 收; stem inferred, perhaps from quri- 'gather') [收了]

sentences.t: Žamuqa-luγ̇a aγsad Žadaran, Qatagin, Salžiγ̇ud, Dörben, Taičiγ̇ud, Uṅgirad kiġed tende-kü oroba.
sentences.l: With Žamuqa having been, the Žadaran, Qatagin, Salžiγud, Dörben, Taičiγud, Uṅgirad and the others there also entered.
sentences.i: The Jadaran, Qatagin, Saljiud, Dörben, Taichi’ud and Ongirad, and the others who had been with Jamuqa, came over there as well.
sentences.n: Žamuqa-luγ̇a aγsad is “those who were with Jamuqa”: -luγ̇a is the comitative (Ming 一同 “together”), and aγsad is a- “be” in a plural past participle. Six peoples are named, each with the Ming’s 種名 “a people’s name”; kiġed “and the others” closes the list. oroba is “entered”, and the Ming 投入了 “threw themselves in” suggests joining, but the text does not say whom they joined; I take it to be Chinggis (uncertain). tende-kü is “there, indeed / also” (Ming 那裏 也).

morph.gloss: Jamuqa, a man's name [人名 一同]
comitative: with (back-vowel form) [人名 一同]
past participle with plural -d: those who were [住來的每]
the Saljiud, a clan (plural in -d) [種名]
the Dörben, a people (the word is 'four') [種名]
the Taichi'ud, a clan (plural in -d) [種名]
the Ongirad, a people (plural in -d) [種名]
emphatic particle: also, indeed (Ming 也) [那裏 也]
to enter, to go in [投入了]

sentences.t: Tajaṅ-un eke Kürbesü-ji Čiṅgis Qaγan abčiraγ̇ulžu ügülerün:
sentences.l: Tajaṅ’s mother Kürbesü-(object), Chinggis Qaγan having had brought, saying:
sentences.i: Chinggis Qahan had Tayang’s mother Kürbesü brought, and said:
sentences.n: abčiraγ̇ulžu is abčira- “bring” with the causative -γ̇ul- (“cause to bring”) and a converb -žu, and the Ming 敎將來着 reads it as “having (someone) bring”. Kürbesü-ji is the accusative; the Ming 母名 行 shows she is a woman. Tajaṅ-un eke is “Tayang’s mother”, genitive -un after a consonant. ügülerün is ügüle- “speak” + -rün, “saying”; the quotation follows.

morph.gloss: Kürbesü, a woman's name (Tayang's mother) [(母)名 行]
accusative: marks the object (after a vowel) [(母)名 行]

sentences.t: "Či Moṅγol-un hünir maγ̇ui keġežü ese-ü büleġe. Edöġe jakin irebe či"
sentences.l: “You, the Mongols’ smell bad saying, not was? Now how came you?”
sentences.i: “You said, ‘The Mongols smell foul,’ did you not? Now how is it that you have come?”
sentences.n: Chinggis speaks to Kürbesü. hünir is “smell, breath” (Ming 氣息), maγ̇ui “bad” (歹). keġežü ese-ü büleġe is “saying, was it not?”: ese is the negative of the past, -ü read as the question particle (the glossary’s reading; here the Ming gives only 不曾, with no 麽, so the question is uncertain), and büleġe is the past of bü- “be” (Ming 有來); the idiom “did you not say” is my reading. jakin “how, why” (如何), irebe “came”. Shiratori marks the quotation, outer double marks, inner single in the idiomatic line.

morph.gloss: the Mongols (the Ming glosses 達達 'Tatars') [達達的]
question particle (the glossary’s reading; here the Ming gives only 不曾, with no 麽; uncertain) [不曾]
past: there was, used to be (Ming 有來) [有來]

sentences.t: keġežü Čiṅgis Qaγan abulaγ̇a.
sentences.l: saying, Chinggis Qaγan took (had taken).
sentences.i: So saying, Chinggis Qahan took her.
sentences.n: keġežü “saying” closes the speech. abulaγ̇a is ab- “take” with the past -laγ̇a (Ming 要了來 “took”, 來 giving the sense of “had taken”). The object is not stated; “her” is supplied from the speech just made to Kürbesü, and the verb, which can also mean “take as a wife”, is left in its plain sense.

morph.gloss: past: -ed (Ming 了來), 'took, had taken' [要了來]

sentences.t: Mün quluγana žil namur Qaradal-Hužaγ̇ur-a Merkid-ün Toγtoγ̇a-Beki-lüġe Čiṅgis Qaγan baildužu
sentences.l: The very mouse year, autumn, at Qaradal-Hužaγur, of the Merkid with Toγtoγa-Beki, Chinggis Qaγan standing against one another,
sentences.i: In the very year of the Rat, in the autumn, at Qaradal-Huja’ur, Chinggis Qahan drew up against Toqto’a-Beki of the Merkid,
sentences.n: §197 opens. Mün quluγana žil is “the very Rat year” (Ming 只 for mün, “just, the very”; the Ming 鼠 “mouse” is the animal, which we call the Rat). baildužu is bai- “stand” + reciprocal -ldu- + converb, “standing against one another”, the Ming 對陣着, “facing in battle line”. Merkid-ün Toγtoγ̇a-Beki-lüġe is “with the Merkid’s Toqto’a-Beki” (comitative -lüġe, front-vowel form; beki is a title of rank). Qaradal-Hužaγ̇ur-a: the place, with the dative-locative -a (Ming 地名 行).

morph.gloss: just, the very (particle; Ming 只) [只]
Qaradal-Hužaγur, a place name (Ming 地名) [地名行]
dative-locative: at, in, to (back-vowel form; the Ming marks it 行) [地名行]
the Merkid, a people [種名 的]
genitive: of (front-vowel form, after a consonant) [種名 的]
Toqto'a, a man's name [人名 一同]
beki, a title of rank [人名 一同]
comitative: with (front-vowel form) [人名 一同]

sentences.t: Toγtoγ̇a-ji ködölgežü Saγ̇ari-Keġer-e irge orγa ulus in-ü daγ̇uliba.
sentences.l: Toγtoγa-(object) setting in motion, at Saγari-Keġer, people, household, realm his seized.
sentences.i: He drove Toqto’a off, and at Sa’ari-Keger seized his people, his household and his realm.
sentences.n: ködölgežü is ködöl- “move” with the causative -ge- and a converb, “making move, setting in motion” (the Ming 推動着 “pushing on”); Toγtoγ̇a-ji is the accusative after a vowel. Saγ̇ari-Keġer-e has the dative-locative -e, “at / to”: whether Toqto’a was driven to Sa’ari-Keger or the booty was taken there I cannot tell from the grammar (uncertain). Three nouns, irge orγa ulus (Ming 百姓, 人烟 “smoke of dwellings”, 國), are the object of daγ̇uliba, “seized”, with in-ü “his” after them.

morph.gloss: Toqto'a, a man's name [人名 行]
accusative: marks the object (after a vowel) [人名 行]
to move, to set out [推動着]
Sa'ari-Keger, a place name (Ming 地名) [地名 行]

sentences.t: Toγtoγ̇a Qudu, Čilaγ̇un köġüd- lüġe-ben čüġen küġün bejes(i)-jen dutaγ̇ažu γarba.
sentences.l: Toγtoγa, Qudu, Čilaγun, sons together-with-own, few man, own persons fleeing went up.
sentences.i: Toqto’a, with his sons Qudu and Chila’un, a few men, and nothing but their own persons, fled and got away.
sentences.n: köġüd- is cut off from lüġe-ben by Shiratori’s hyphen at the line end; köġüd is “sons” (köġün + plural -d, Ming 子每), so Qudu and Chila’un are Toqto’a’s sons, with lüġe-ben “together with (their) own”. bejes(i)-jen is beje “body” + plural -s (the Ming 罄身(每) “bare person(s)”) + reflexive -jen, “their own persons”: they escaped with nothing else. dutaγ̇ažu γarba is “fleeing, went out/up”, here “got away”.

plural (Ming 每; uncertain) [罄身(每)自的行]

sentences.t: Tedüi Merkid irgen daγ̇uliγdarun Γoγ̇as-Merkid-ün Dair-Usun öki-jen Qulan-Qatun-i Čiṅgis Qaγan-(n)a üžeġülsü keġen abču aisurun
sentences.l: Those Merkid people when plundered, of the Γoγas Merkid Dair-Usun daughter-own Qulan Qatun-(object), to Chinggis Qaγan let me present saying, taking, when coming,
sentences.i: When those Merkid people were being plundered, Dair-Usun of the Qo’as Merkid was bringing his own daughter, Lady Qulan, saying, “Let me present her to Chinggis Qahan,” and was on his way;
sentences.n: daγ̇uliγdarun is daγ̇uli- “plunder” + passive -γda- + -run, “when plundered” (Ming 被據時). Γoγ̇as-Merkid-ün: the Ming 姓(名) 種名 的 gives “clan-name, a people’s, of”. öki-jen is “his own daughter”, and Qulan-Qatun-i is accusative. üžeġülsü is üžeġül- “present, offer up” (Ming 獻與) with the first-person optative -sü, “let me present”, closing in keġen, “saying”. The stem üžeġül- is not secure. Shiratori prints no quotation marks here; the quotation marks in the idiomatic line are mine.

people, the common folk of a camp or realm [百姓]
to plunder, to carry off [被據時]

sentences.t: žaγ̇ura čeriġüd-te žedgügdežü Baγ̇aridai Najā nojan-dur učiražu
sentences.l: On the road by soldiers being obstructed, the Baγaridai Najā noyan-to meeting,
sentences.i: On the road he was stopped by soldiers and met the noyan Naya’a of the Ba’aridai,
sentences.n: žedgügdežü is a passive converb, “being obstructed”, from a stem žedgü- inferred from the Ming 當着 “withstand”; čeriġüd-te is the soldiers with -te, here marking the agent. Baγ̇aridai (Ming 種名) is a people’s name, though the glossary has read it as a man’s name; Najā is a short writing of Najaγ̇a, which §197 uses further on. nojan-dur is “to / with the noyan” (Ming 官人行), and učiražu “meeting”.

sentences.t: Dair-Usun ügülerün: "Ene öki-jen Čiṅgis Qaγan-(n)a üžeġülsü keġen aisu. bi" keġežüġüi.
sentences.l: Dair-Usun saying: “This daughter-own to Chinggis Qaγan let me present saying, I come. I” said.
sentences.i: Dair-Usun said: “I am on my way to present this daughter of mine to Chinggis Qahan.”
sentences.n: Dair-Usun’s answer, with Shiratori’s marks from Ene to bi. The Mongol is “this daughter of mine, to Chinggis Qaγan ‘let me present’ saying, [I] am coming”: aisu is a stem whose ending is unclear (the Ming 來有 is “there is coming”) and the bi after Shiratori’s full stop is the pronoun “I”, falling oddly at the end, which I take as part of the same sentence. keġežüġüi “[he] said” only repeats ügülerün and is left out of the idiomatic line.

sentences.t: Tende Najā nojan ügülerün: "Ökin-i čin-u bida. qamtu üžeġülüje" keġen töridġežüġüi.
sentences.l: There Najā noyan saying: “Girl-(object) your, we together let us present” saying, stopped (him).
sentences.i: Then Naya’a the noyan said: “Let us two present your daughter together,” and stopped him.
sentences.n: ökin-i čin-u bida qamtu üžeġülüje is “the girl, yours, we together let us present”: bida is the inclusive “we” (you and I; the Ming 咱), and -üje is the hortative “let us”, so the two of them would present her. Shiratori puts a full stop after bida, which I take as a slip. töridġežüġüi is a past of a stem töridġe- inferred from the Ming 止住了 “stopped”; the object, Dair-Usun, is understood.

morph.gloss: accusative: marks the object (after a consonant) [女子行]

sentences.t: "Töridgerün Dair-Usun-i či γaγčaγ̇ar oduγ̇asu žaγ̇ura čeriġüd samaγ̇ui čaγ-tur čima-ji ber ülü aγ̇ulqu öki taki čin-u samaγ̇uraqu"
sentences.l: “When stopping Dair-Usun-(object), you alone if going, on the road soldiers disorderly time-at, you-(object) even not will make live; daughter also your will be in disorder”
sentences.i: While he held Dair-Usun back he said: “If you go alone at a time when the soldiers on the road are in disorder, they will not spare even you, and your daughter too will be thrown into confusion”
sentences.n: Shiratori’s opening mark stands on Töridgerün, “when stopping”, and Dair-Usun-i is its object (accusative, as the Ming 人名行 marks it): “when stopping Dair-Usun”. Both belong to the narration, so I take the speech to begin at či and Shiratori’s mark to be two words early (uncertain; it could instead be a vocative “Dair-Usun, …”, which the accusative does not favour). The l keeps Shiratori’s mark, the i puts it where the speech begins. Then the speech: oduγ̇asu is “if (you) go” (conditional -uγ̇asu, Ming 去呵), samaγ̇ui čaγ-tur “at the time of disorder”. aγ̇ulqu is a- “be, live” + causative -γ̇ul- + participle, “will make live”, so with ülü “will not spare” (Ming 敎活). samaγ̇uraqu “will be in disorder” is said of the daughter as well as of the soldiers; for her I render “thrown into confusion”, a euphemism I have not pinned down (uncertain).

sentences.t: keġežü γurban üdür γurban süni töridġežüġüi.
sentences.l: saying, three days three nights stopped (him).
sentences.i: So saying, he kept him there three days and three nights.
sentences.n: keġežü “saying” ends Naya’a’s speech; töridġežüġüi is the same “stopped” as before. The Mongol puts the numbers before the nouns: γurban üdür γurban süni, “three day, three night”; a number before a singular noun is the norm.

morph.gloss: to stop, to hold back [止住了有]

sentences.t: Tendēče Qulan Qatun-luγ̇a Dair-Usun-i abuγ̇ad qamtu Najā nojan Čiṅgis Qaγan-dur kürgebe.
sentences.l: From there Qulan Qatun-with Dair-Usun-(object) having taken, together, Najā noyan to Chinggis Qaγan delivered.
sentences.i: From there Naya’a the noyan took Dair-Usun together with Lady Qulan, and delivered them to Chinggis Qahan.
sentences.n: Tendēče is tende “there” with the ablative -ēče. Qatun-luγ̇a is the comitative, “with the lady”, and Dair-Usun-i the accusative, so Naya’a takes Dair-Usun with Qulan; abuγ̇ad “having taken”, qamtu “together”. kürgebe is kürge- “bring to, deliver” (kür- “reach” made causative, uncertain) in the past; the Ming 到了 is “arrived”. I render Qatun as “Lady” in the idiomatic line.

accusative: marks the object (after a consonant) [人名行]
dative-locative: at, in, to (back-vowel form) [皇帝 行]
to bring to, to deliver (kür- 'reach' made causative; uncertain) [到了]

sentences.t: Tendēče Čiṅgis Qaγan Najā-ji "jakin tödeġežü aba či" keġen
sentences.l: From there Chinggis Qaγan, Najā-(object): “How stopping dwelt you?” saying,
sentences.i: Then Chinggis Qahan said to Naya’a: “Why did you stop and stay?”
sentences.n: Najā-ji is the accusative of the one addressed, here “said to Naya’a”; it may equally be the object of asaγču in the next unit (“questioned Naya’a”). jakin “how, why” (Ming 如何). tödeġežü aba is “stopping, dwelt”: tödeġe- is a stem inferred from the Ming 止當着 “stop, hold up” and may be related to töridġe-; aba is a- “dwell” in the past (Ming 住了). “Stop and stay” is my reading of the pair, not a certainty.

morph.gloss: accusative: marks the object (after a vowel) [人名行]
to stop, to hold up (stem inferred from the Ming 止當着; perhaps related to töridġe-) [止當着]

sentences.t: maši kiliṅlažu qataṅγuj-a maraγ̇an asaγču "Žasaγ bolγaja" keġen asaγun büküi-dür
sentences.l: much angry, with sternness minutely asking: “Law let us make” saying asking, at the being,
sentences.i: Greatly angry, he questioned him sternly and closely, saying, “Let us make a ruling,” and as he questioned him,
sentences.n: Another converb chain: kiliṅlažu “being angry” (stem read from the Ming 怒), asaγču “asking”, with qataṅγuj-a, “with sternness” (the Ming 剛硬 行, hard, with the -a read as an adverbial dative-locative; the form is not secure) and maraγ̇an “closely, minutely”. “Žasaγ bolγaja” is žasaγ “law, regulation” (Ming 法度) + bol- “become” + causative -γa- + hortative -ja, “let us make law”: whether this means “let us make a ruling”, “let us apply the law” or something else I am not sure. büküi-dür is bü- “be” + participle -küi + dative-locative, “at the being, while” (Ming 有時).

morph.gloss: to be angry (stem inferred from the Ming 怒) [怒着]
hard, stern, unyielding (Ming 剛硬; the form is uncertain) [剛硬 行]
dative-locative, used adverbially: 'with sternness' (Ming 行) [剛硬 行]
law, regulation, discipline (Ming 法度) [法度]
dative-locative: at, in, to (front-vowel form) [有 時]

sentences.t: Qulan qatun ügülerün: "Najaγ̇a ügüleleġe.
sentences.l: Qulan Qatun saying: “Najaγa had said.
sentences.i: Lady Qulan said: “Naya’a said this.
sentences.n: Qulan Qatun’s speech runs from here to the closing mark on asaγasuγ̇asu. Najaγ̇a ügüleleġe is “Naya’a had said”: -leġe is a past (the Ming 說來 “said”, 來 marking a completed past). Shiratori puts a full stop, but what follows are Naya’a’s words, quoted inside hers without marks; I add single marks in the idiomatic lines. Najaγ̇a is the full spelling of the Najā met earlier.

morph.gloss: lady, queen, wife of a khan [娘子]

sentences.t: Čiṅgis Qaγan-(n)u jeke nojan bijü bi.
sentences.l: Chinggis Qaγan’s great noyan there is, I.
sentences.i: ‘I am a great noyan of Chinggis Qahan.
sentences.n: Naya’a’s words as Qulan reports them. bijü is the present “there is” of bü- (Ming 有), followed by bi “I” (我); I read the two together as “I am”, though “there is a great noyan of Chinggis Qaγan: I” is the literal order and the sense is the same. jeke nojan is “great noyan” (大官人).

morph.gloss: genitive: of (back-vowel form; the (n) is Shiratori’s, printed after a stem that already ends in n) [皇帝 的]
to be; present bijü, 'there is' (Ming 有) [有]

sentences.t: Bida qamtu öki čin-u qaγan-(n)a üžeġülüje.
sentences.l: We together daughter your to the qan let us present.
sentences.i: Let us two together present your daughter to the Qahan.’
sentences.n: The same hortative as before: bida “we (you and I)” + qamtu “together” + üžeġülüje “let us present”, with öki čin-u, “daughter yours”, as the object, and qaγan-(n)a, “to the qan” (the dative-locative, Ming 皇帝 行). The idiomatic line closes Naya’a’s first utterance with a single mark.

to present, to offer up [共獻咱]

sentences.t: Žaγ̇ura čeriġüd samaγ̇uraqu keġen idγaluγ̇a.
sentences.l: On the road soldiers will be in disorder, saying, urged.
sentences.i: ‘On the road the soldiers will run riot,’ he urged us.
sentences.n: samaγ̇uraqu is the “will be in disorder” of the earlier speech (Ming 作亂 “make disorder”). idγaluγ̇a is idγa- “urge, persuade” (stem read from the Ming 勸) with a past -luγ̇a (as -laγ̇a; Ming 來); the object is not stated, and “us” is supplied as Qulan’s side.

sentences.t: Edöġe Najaγ̇a-dāča busud čeriġüd-tür učiraγ̇asu Samaγ̇u-dur čeküi-dür Oroqu-ju ažuγ̇u. γai.
sentences.l: Now Najaγa-from other soldiers-to if meeting, in disorder, in rawness entering was, I do not know.
sentences.i: Now, if we had met soldiers other than Naya’a’s, we should have gone into the disorder, into the unfamiliar, who knows?
sentences.n: Qulan speaks for herself. Najaγ̇a-dāča is “from Naya’a” (the Ming 處 “at the place of”), which I take as “other than Naya’a”; busud čeriġüd is “the other soldiers”. učiraγ̇asu is the conditional “if meeting”. oroqu-ju ažuγ̇u is “entering is, was”, i.e. “would have entered”; the -ju is read from the Ming 有 and is uncertain. samaγ̇u-dur čeküi-dür is “in disorder, in čeküi”: čeküi (Ming 生裏, 生 “raw, unripe, strange”) I cannot read with confidence and render “the unfamiliar”. γai is the Ming 不知 “I do not know”.

sentences.t: Ene Najaγ̇a-dur učiraqui man-u sain bolba.
sentences.l: This Najaγa-to meeting our good became.
sentences.i: Our meeting with Naya’a has turned out well for us.
sentences.n: učiraqui is the participle “the meeting” (Ming 的); Najaγ̇a-dur is the dative-locative, “with Naya’a”. man-u sain bolba is “our good became”, with man-u the genitive of ba “we”, which I take as exclusive from its form man- (the Ming alternates 俺 and 咱 and does not itself mark the difference), contrasted with the inclusive bida just above. A fine pair for the learner: bida includes the person spoken to, man-u does not.

morph.gloss: Naya'a, a man's name [人名 行]
dative-locative: at, in, to (back-vowel form) [人名 行]
to meet, to chance upon [遇着的]
participle: that which …, 'the meeting' (Ming 的) [遇着的]

sentences.t: Edöġe Najaγ̇a-dāča asaγtala Qaγan sojurγaγ̇asu teṅgeri-jin žajaγ̇a-γ̇ar ečige eke töreġülügsen marijan-(n)ača asaγasuγ̇asu" keġen öčiġülžüġüi.
sentences.l: Now Najaγa-from while asking, the Qaγan if favouring, Heaven’s by destiny father mother caused to be born skin-from if asking,” saying, had it reported.
sentences.i: “Now, as the Qahan questions Naya’a, if he should graciously ask him from the skin that his father and mother bore him by Heaven’s destiny,” so saying, she had it reported.
sentences.n: A hard sentence; the reading is tentative. asaγtala is asaγ- “ask” + -tala “while” (Ming 問間), active: the asker is the Qahan, supplied from the next clause, and Najaγ̇a-dāča “from / of Naya’a” is what he asks. sojurγaγ̇asu is “if (he) favours” (Ming 恩賜呵). Teṅgeri-jin žajaγ̇a-γ̇ar is “by Heaven’s destiny”; ečige eke töreġülügsen marijan-(n)ača is “from the skin that father (and) mother caused to be born”, i.e. ask from my very person, as when we say “on one’s life”, which is a guess at an idiom. asaγasuγ̇asu is “if (he) asks”, the -su- unexplained. “Had it reported” translates öčiġülžüġüi (Ming 敎奏了), a causative of öči- “report”; I do not know to whom.

sentences.t: Najaγ̇a asaγdarun:
sentences.l: Najaγa when asked:
sentences.i: Questioned, Naya’a said:
sentences.n: asaγdarun is asaγ- “ask” + passive -da- + -run, “when asked” (Ming 被問時). The speech follows, with Shiratori’s opening mark on Qaγan-(n)ača; “said” is supplied from the colon.

sentences.t: "Qaγan-(n)ača busu niγ̇ur min-u ügei bi-že.
sentences.l: “From the Qaγan other face mine there is not indeed.
sentences.i: “Apart from the Qahan I have no other face, truly.
sentences.n: Qaγan-(n)ača is the ablative “from, than”, busu niγ̇ur min-u ügei, “other face mine without”. The assertion particle -že (in bi-že, Ming 有也者) makes it “truly”. The sense of “face” here, honour or standing before others, is mine and not the glossators’.

sentences.t: Qari irgen-ü qačar γoγ̇a öki qatun qarγam sain aγta učiraγ̇asu Qaγan-(n)u-γ̇an kü keġežü amu-že bi.
sentences.l: Foreign people’s cheek fair girl lady, haunch good gelding if meeting, own Qaγan indeed saying, am indeed, I.
sentences.i: If I come upon a fair-cheeked girl or lady of a foreign people, or a gelding with fine haunches, I say, ‘Surely they are my own Qahan’s.’
sentences.n: Qari irgen-ü is “of the foreign people” (Ming 外邦 百姓), qačar γoγ̇a “cheek fair”, i.e. fair-cheeked, öki qatun “girl, lady”, and qarγam sain aγta “haunch good gelding”. učiraγ̇asu “if meeting”. Qaγan-(n)u-γ̇an kü is “of one’s own Qaγan, indeed”; keġežü amu-že bi is “saying, I am indeed”, I take as “I say”. amu is uncertain: the Ming 有 suggests a present of a- “be”, and I have not pinned the ending down.

sentences.t: Eġün-eče busu sedkil min-u böġesü üküšü bi" keġežüġüi.
sentences.l: This-than other heart mine if be, die let me I” saying said.
sentences.i: If my heart is other than this, may I die!” So he said.
sentences.n: Eġün-eče is “than this” (the Ming 比這箇行: a comparative ablative), busu sedkil min-u böġesü “other heart mine if it be”, with the conditional -ġesü of bü-. üküšü is ükü- “die” in the optative first person, “let me die” (Ming 死我). The closing mark is on bi.

morph.gloss: this one (the oblique stem of ene) [比這箇行]

sentences.t: Čiṅgis Qaγan Qulan Qatun-(n)u öčil žöbšiježü
sentences.l: Chinggis Qaγan, of Qulan Qatun the report approving,
sentences.i: Chinggis Qahan, approving Lady Qulan’s report,
sentences.n: öčil is “what is reported up” (the Ming 奏事 “a memorial”): the “report” or “petition” Qulan had made. žöbšiježü is “approving” (the Ming 道是着, stem žöbšiye- “to agree to”). Qulan Qatun-(n)u is a genitive on the title.

sentences.t: mün üdür(i)-jer böġed bolγan soriγ̇asu
sentences.l: that very day then, making testing-if,
sentences.i: and, making trial of it that very day,
sentences.n: mün üdür(i)-jer is “on the very day” (the Ming 日裏 “within the day”, -jer being an ending of uncertain force with the shape of the instrumental). böġed (Ming 便) is “then”. bolγan soriγ̇asu is “making testing-if”: sori- is a stem inferred from the Ming 試 “try”. The Ming glosses bolγan 審 “scrutinise”, but the glossary reads bolγan as bol- plus causative, “making”, and I keep “making” in both lines rather than add “carefully”; the Ming’s nuance is uncertain.

sentences.t: Qulan qatun-(n)u öčil adali boldažu
sentences.l: Qulan Qatun’s report alike being made,
sentences.i: found Lady Qulan’s report to tally,
sentences.n: adali boldažu is “being made alike”, the Ming 相似 被做着: that is, found to agree. With what is not said: I take it to be with the facts and Naya’a’s account, since the next unit sets Naya’a’s words beside it.

sentences.t: Čiṅgis Qaγan Qulan qatun-(n)i sojurγažu taγ̇alaba.
sentences.l: Chinggis Qaγan Qulan Qatun-(object) favouring, loved.
sentences.i: Chinggis Qahan showed favour to Lady Qulan and loved her.
sentences.n: sojurγažu is sojurγa- “show favour” (Ming 恩賜) with the converb -žu; taγ̇alaba is taγ̇ala- “love” (Ming 愛) in the past. The accusative is -(n)i, with the Ming 行. The Qulan of §197 is, by the Ming’s 女名 and 娘子, a woman and a Qatun.

sentences.t: Najaγ̇a-jin üges adali boldažu žöbšiježü
sentences.l: Najaγa’s words alike being made, approving,
sentences.i: Naya’a’s words tallied too, and approving them,
sentences.n: The same pattern as the unit for Qulan’s report: üges “words” (üge + plural -s, Ming 言語每), adali boldažu “being made alike”, žöbšiježü “approving”. The genitive is -jin after a vowel.

morph.gloss: to be made, to become [被做着]
to approve, to agree to [道是着]

sentences.t: "ünen ügetü ažuγ̇u" keġen "jeke üile tüšišü" keġen sojurγaba.
sentences.l: “True word-having was” saying, “great matter let me entrust” saying, bestowed favour.
sentences.i: he said, “He was a man of true word,” and “I will entrust him with a great charge,” and showed him favour.
sentences.n: ünen ügetü is “true, word-having” (Ming 眞實 言語有的), -tü being the possessive “having”, so a man of true word. tüšišü is tüši- “entrust, appoint” (stem inferred from the Ming 委付) with the first-person optative -šü, “let me entrust”; the one entrusted is not named, and “him” (Naya’a) is supplied. Shiratori’s marks are on each of the two sayings; sojurγaba is the same “showed favour” as above, in the past.
